newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota, GM Australia units mull cut in supply link.
newsitem.headline: Toyota, GM Australia units mull cut in supply link.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp is in talks with General Motors Corp (GM) about stopping supplying each other with cars in Australia, a Toyota spokesman said on Friday.
In March, Toyota and GM dissolved their Australian joint venture, United Australian Automotive Industries Ltd, under which the two supplied their Australian-made cars to each other.
Toyota stopped supplying its Australian unit-made Corollas to the Australian unit of General Motors Corp in April.
Toyota Motor Australia Ltd (TMA) supplied the Corollas to GM's Australian unit General Motors-Holden's Automotive Ltd (GMA) for sale under the name Nova.
TMA still supplies Camry cars to GM for sale as Apollos, and GMA supplies Commodores to TMA for sale as the Lexcen.
They are in talks to cease supplying the models soon, the spokesman said.
Toyota supplied 3,600 Novas and 2,800 Apollos to GM in 1995 and GM's Australian unit supplied 5,600 Commodores to TMA.
